title: In the Soft Season of Thy Youth
description: In the Soft Season of Thy Youth in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Gibbons wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 742 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the soft sea-son of thy youth, In Na-ture's smil-ing bloom, Ere age ar-rive, and trem-bling wait Its sum-mons to the tomb;

lines: In the soft season of thy youth,
Ere age arrive, and trembling wait
Make him thy fear, thy love, thy hope,
He shall defend and guide thy course
Till thou art landed on the shore
Then seek the Lord betimes, and choose
The earth affords no lovelier sight

licence: Public domain: Thomas Gibbons died in 1785.
credits: Words by Thomas Gibbons (1720–1785), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
